question: Re-judgement of 26.09 (SCORECARD §0): criterion 8.2 Range 7.5 / 15, the largest gap: '1 STOP frame beyond 100 m on the organizers' objects; 0.3 m cubes at 43-53 m'. On set O (cloud_with_fake_obj, scored with scripts/score_fake_objects.py): big_center first STOP 98.0 m (held from 98.7), big_above first STOP 101.3 m but held only from 23.9 m (on wf14/integrate-p3; no hold on 00143b0), long_low_on_rails first STOP 82.2 m (held 90.8), small_center 52.5 m, small_on_rail 42.7 m, thin_hanging 30.1 m. What limits the first STOP / hold distance: physics (too few returns) or a config limit / rule (returns present but rejected)? Ship a range gain only through this pre-registration.

investigation.code: 00143b0 (claude/nifty-pascal-lzgl78), default config, native path, receive stamps, every frame; no rule changed (instrumented replays whose wrappers only record: the output is the default's)
investigation.method: Set O: the organizers' object points are the tail of every cached frame (the ray-cast block appended after the real scan, scripts/label_fake_objects.py), so per object and frame the returns are known exactly; a replay with recording wrappers around Detector._corridor, clustering._corridor_cluster, clustering._low_cluster, detector.find_clusters and detector.find_hanging logs, per object-frame: the returns, how many lie in the corridor (advisory zone) and in the strict envelope (edge margin applied), the valid / axis / height-reference ranges, every blob holding object points with the stage's decision (dropped by oversize / min_height / min_points / infrastructure, or kept with zone and demotion reason), the track it fed (hits, confidence, zone vote, reported) and the decision. Real data: the same wrappers over the six recordings and the ride (new_data, 8 pieces as the gate) log every corridor blob with a strict-envelope voxel beyond 40 m and every `elevated` blob, plus per frame the returns within 0.9 m of the axis at 100-200 m just above the envelope top (3.0-3.6 m) and just below its floor (-0.5-0.12 m). Scripts: scratch (trace_setO.py, trace_pop.py), not committed.

false_alarm_cost_of_relaxing.reading: Relaxing the envelope beyond the bed range, or admitting flat or 3-4 voxel clusters as new tracks, would add candidates on about half of the ride's frames at 100-200 m: the far limits on set O objects are the height reference's, and they hold back real clutter. What is cheap is hysteresis on a track already confirmed: on the real data the shape signatures almost never hit a STOP track (1 logged cluster-frame on the ride beyond 40 m), while on set O they take the box at the envelope top down.

rules.tracking.stop_keep_signature: bool, false = off (today). true: a track reported as an obstacle (STOP, zone gauge) in the previous frame counts a hit whose cluster has >= gauge_min_points voxels inside the strict gauge but was demoted only by a shape signature (elevated, floating, edge, wall_face; clustering.SHAPE_SIGNATURES) as a hit inside the gauge in its zone vote. Never a column (the column hold), beyond_axis, beyond_height_ref, overhead or retro. It never makes a new obstacle: an unreported or advisory track votes as today. Reported reason 'stop_hold'. Geometry-general: a shape heuristic for infrastructure may keep a track from being confirmed; it does not take a confirmed obstacle down.
rules.tracking.stop_keep_thin: int, 0 = off (today). The corridor clusters flatter than cluster.min_height (one scan line), which are dropped today, are kept aside (Cluster.thin; no other stage sees them) and, after the association of the ordinary clusters, may continue a track that nothing matched, greedily with the same gate and prediction, when they are inside the gauge (zone gauge; or demoted by a shape signature for a STOP track with stop_keep_signature). 1: only a track reported as an obstacle in the previous frame (it cannot confirm anything new). 2: also a track not yet reported whose last hit was inside the gauge (the scan line counts towards its confirmation). A thin cluster never starts a track.

preregistered.expected_from_the_investigation: A: big_above STOP held to ~48 m, then the track dies in the single-ring frames (no held-from gain alone). B: big_above held from ~101 m to the end (held-from 23.9 -> ~101 m on the integrated base), long_low one more STOP frame (75.4 m). C: in addition big_above's first STOP may move from 101.3 to ~109.5 m and long_low's from 82.2 to ~83.8 m. Other objects: no change expected. The false-alarm side is unknown: A and B can only extend STOPs that exist (alarm frames), C can also confirm new tracks.

stages.cheap: scripts/regression_gate.py --cache <a directory of symlinks to the six recordings and cloud_with_fake_obj, no new_data> --jobs 1 --baseline <the current baseline> --allow 'ride.*' --allow 'set_F_straight.*' --set <candidate>; first on 00143b0 + flags (baseline _ride_p3b), then, after the merge of wf14/integrate-p3, on the merged head (baseline _ride_p3c). Pass = exit 0 and the five recordings' alarm frames not up and the set O minimum gain below.
stages.full: the same with --cache /data/cache (the ride in 8 pieces, set F straight round 3), no --allow, against docs/evidence/results/regression_baseline_2026-09-26_ride_p3c.json on the merged head, only for a candidate that passed the cheap stage on the merged head.
stages.order: All three through the cheap stage in the order A, B, C. To the full gate goes the candidate with the largest set O gain among those passing the cheap stage (sum over inside objects of the gains in first-STOP and held-from distance; a tie goes to the earlier candidate); if it fails, the next one, time permitting (the verdict is committed by 13:30 UTC; a full gate that cannot finish by then is not started, and nothing ships).

ship_rule.gate: the full gate exits 0 with no --allow: no gated row worse or missing
ship_rule.ride: ride alarm frames, alarm events and STOP episodes each not up (alarm frames is an information row of the gate; it is a ship condition here: a range rule must not add false STOP frames on the ride)
ship_rule.five_recordings: alarm frames, alarm events and STOP episodes each not up (summed and per recording)
ship_rule.doubleT_obstacle: first alarm frame not later, labelled hits per label not down, false-alarm events not up
ship_rule.set_F_straight: per kind sequences detected not down, median first confirmation not shorter, false detections not up
ship_rule.set_O_safety: every inside object's STOP frames not down and first STOP not nearer; outside objects' false STOP frames and background alarm frames / track ids not up (gated rows)
ship_rule.set_O_minimum_gain: at least one inside object's held-from or first-STOP distance (score_fake_objects.py) grows by >= 10 m, or at least two inside objects' grow by >= 1 m each
ship_rule.then: ship = the candidate's values become the defaults in configs/default.yaml (and the ROS parameter file via scripts/sync_params.sh); otherwise the flags stay off and the candidates are recorded as tried, not shipped
ship_rule.priority: safety wins over false-alarm gains; a range gain must not add false STOPs on the ride
